I'm getting −0.7435% gain error per transfer by following the original Phillips patents (US3546490, US3745383) and Sangster’s 1970 Philips tetrode paper.
```
donor bucket -- isolation MOS -- MID -- clocked MOS -- recipient bucket
                    |                      |                 |
                 DC bias                 clock           storage C
                                                             |
                                                        plate drive
```
That's... a lot. Commercial BBDs have [-2 dB to +2 dB insertion loss], with (I assume) some internal buffering to account for the positive gain.

Right now I'm trying (even larger) time gaps in break-before-make, but there is no improvement.

Is this about transistor sizes? Are commercial BBDs on a different PDK? Any ideas?
